fix(parser): parse ALTER TABLE DROP with multiple columns (#8486)

* fix(parser): parse ALTER TABLE DROP with multiple columns

ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN a, b fell back to parsing as a Command
because only the first column was consumed and the comma-separated
continuation had no DROP keyword for the CSV action parser to match.

Parse the continuation columns as additional Drop actions with the
same kind. (GH#8485)

* fix(parser): keep multi-column DROP COLUMN in one action per dialect flag

Per the review on GH#8486, splitting `ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN a, b`
into separate Drop actions broke three things: Snowflake and T-SQL
reject the generated `DROP COLUMN a, DROP COLUMN b` with a syntax
error, calling `_parse_drop_column` directly skipped MySQL's
`_parse_alter_drop_action` (so `DROP PRIMARY KEY` became a Command),
and MySQL options after a DROP got parsed as columns (`DROP COLUMN a,
ALGORITHM=INPLACE` raised a ParseError).

Follow the `ALTER_TABLE_ADD_REQUIRED_FOR_EACH_COLUMN` pattern: add an
`ALTER_TABLE_DROP_REQUIRED_FOR_EACH_COLUMN` flag (False for Snowflake
and T-SQL). In the base `_parse_alter_drop_action`, when the flag is
off and the action is a `DROP COLUMN` followed by a comma, parse the
rest into the same `exp.Drop`'s `tables`, like `DROP TABLE a, b`.
`_parse_alter_table_drop` stays as is, and `drop_sql` round-trips the
result as-is.

Tests: the multi-column identities moved to test_snowflake.py /
test_tsql.py, `DROP COLUMN a, ALGORITHM=INPLACE` and a DropPrimaryKey
action assertion were added to test_mysql.py, and the generic parser
test now asserts a single exp.Drop with multiple tables.

* style: fix ruff-format violation in multi-column DROP test

Wrap the chained assert_is call in test_mysql.py the way ruff format
expects; the previous wrapping was rejected by the ruff-format hook in
'make style' (Makefile:120, pre-commit run --all-files). Formatting
only - no behavioral change.

fix(parser): parse ALTER TABLE DROP with multiple columns (#8486)

* fix(parser): parse ALTER TABLE DROP with multiple columns

ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN a, b fell back to parsing as a Command
because only the first column was consumed and the comma-separated
continuation had no DROP keyword for the CSV action parser to match.

Parse the continuation columns as additional Drop actions with the
same kind. (GH#8485)

* fix(parser): keep multi-column DROP COLUMN in one action per dialect flag

Per the review on GH#8486, splitting `ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN a, b`
into separate Drop actions broke three things: Snowflake and T-SQL
reject the generated `DROP COLUMN a, DROP COLUMN b` with a syntax
error, calling `_parse_drop_column` directly skipped MySQL's
`_parse_alter_drop_action` (so `DROP PRIMARY KEY` became a Command),
and MySQL options after a DROP got parsed as columns (`DROP COLUMN a,
ALGORITHM=INPLACE` raised a ParseError).

Follow the `ALTER_TABLE_ADD_REQUIRED_FOR_EACH_COLUMN` pattern: add an
`ALTER_TABLE_DROP_REQUIRED_FOR_EACH_COLUMN` flag (False for Snowflake
and T-SQL). In the base `_parse_alter_drop_action`, when the flag is
off and the action is a `DROP COLUMN` followed by a comma, parse the
rest into the same `exp.Drop`'s `tables`, like `DROP TABLE a, b`.
`_parse_alter_table_drop` stays as is, and `drop_sql` round-trips the
result as-is.

Tests: the multi-column identities moved to test_snowflake.py /
test_tsql.py, `DROP COLUMN a, ALGORITHM=INPLACE` and a DropPrimaryKey
action assertion were added to test_mysql.py, and the generic parser
test now asserts a single exp.Drop with multiple tables.

* style: fix ruff-format violation in multi-column DROP test

Wrap the chained assert_is call in test_mysql.py the way ruff format
expects; the previous wrapping was rejected by the ruff-format hook in
'make style' (Makefile:120, pre-commit run --all-files). Formatting
only - no behavioral change.
